title: South India's Travel Market Takes Centre Stage at TTF Hyderabad 2026
excerpt: The Travel & Tourism Fair returns to Hyderabad's HITEX Exhibition Centre October 9–11 with 150+ exhibitors, opening to the public on the final day and a half.
body:
• TTF Hyderabad 2026 runs October 9–11 at Hall 2 of the HITEX Exhibition Centre, organized by Fairfest Media — India's oldest and largest travel trade show network — with 150+ exhibitors from 15+ Indian states and 4 countries expected, plus 5,000+ trade professionals.
  • The show is a hybrid B2B/B2C format: trade access throughout the three days, with consumers admitted during the final day and a half.
  • Planning a winter trip? The fair opens to the public on October 10 (2–6 pm) and October 11 (11 am–6 pm) — pre-registration is free, on-spot entry is ₹50, and exhibitors typically offer show-only deals on packages.
  • Fairfest is positioning Hyderabad as South India's key travel-trade gateway, connecting Telangana and Andhra Pradesh with demand for domestic leisure, short-haul holidays, and cultural tourism.

South India's travel market takes center stage this week as the Travel & Tourism Fair (TTF) returns to Hyderabad from October 9 to 11 at Hall 2 of the HITEX Exhibition Centre. Organized by Kolkata-based Fairfest Media, TTF is India's oldest and largest travel trade show network, and the Hyderabad edition is billed as southern India's key business-to-business travel platform.

The 2026 edition is expected to draw 150-plus exhibitors — tourism boards, hotels, resorts, destination management companies, tour operators, travel companies, attractions, and travel technology providers — from more than 15 Indian states and four countries, alongside 5,000-plus trade professionals. The exhibitor mix spans leisure, pilgrimage, group, corporate, and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions) segments.

Why South India, why now

Fairfest's pitch for Hyderabad rests on the region's travel economics: the city is described in the organizer's 2026–27 program as "a major gateway to Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, with strong demand for domestic leisure travel, short-haul holidays, and cultural tourism." The fair is timed deliberately ahead of the festive and winter travel season, when Indian families book their biggest trips of the year.

"TTF Hyderabad continues to reaffirm its status as South India's premier travel trade platform," Fairfest Media chairman and CEO Sanjiv Agarwal said at the close of last year's edition, noting that the show had "spotlighted the rich cultural and tourism potential of Telangana and beyond."

How to attend

The fair runs a hybrid format: trade visitors get access across all three days, while consumers can walk in during the final day and a half — October 10 from 2 pm to 6 pm, and October 11 from 11 am to 6 pm, according to the event listing. Pre-registration is complimentary; on-spot entry costs ₹50. For travelers, the consumer days are the draw: exhibitors routinely roll out show-only discounts on holiday packages, making it one of the cheaper windows of the year to lock in winter travel.

The bigger circuit

TTF Hyderabad is one stop on Fairfest's regional circuit, which runs through Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Delhi, Hyderabad, Patna, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Chennai before culminating in OTM, ranked as India's top travel trade show. The regional fairs function as feeder markets — connecting state tourism boards and local operators with the national industry — and Hyderabad's edition has grown into the anchor event for the southern market.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs planning winter trips home, the timing is practical: the fair lands just as the October–January travel season opens, and the South India focus means strong representation from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh tourism boards — useful for anyone building an itinerary around Hyderabad, Tirupati, or the temple circuits of the region. The inauguration is expected to draw senior government officials and tourism board representatives, underscoring how seriously states now take the trade-show channel for tourism revenue.

What's next

Watch the footfall numbers after October 11 — they are the industry's early read on winter-season demand. With domestic leisure travel still growing and short-haul international trips rebounding, the deals struck on the HITEX floor this weekend will shape what Indian travelers pay for the holiday season.
nri_angle: NRIs planning winter trips home get a practical booking window: the fair's consumer days (Oct 10–11) land at the start of the holiday travel season, with strong Telangana and Andhra Pradesh representation for South India itineraries.
